tags.gist: Calls the two axes sound but says activity placement rests on assertion; what the generative component may architecturally write and initiate is more auditable.
Recommends basing activity-axis placement, as claimed and verified, on the write authority of the generative component.
Wants S.3 to separate computed from generated confidence, treating generated confidence passed off as computed as a failure, plus a new Record Integrity element.
Would tie competency evidence to a fingerprint of the whole deployed build; any fingerprint change, including third-party model changes, triggers re-benchmarking.
Finds postmarket reliance defensible only where the record being monitored is honest by construction, supervisory agents held to the same partition and a passivity test.
For agentic devices, wants irreversible-action gates acting on witnessed state, acts logged with consequences, stops as reflexes, and an audit log the agent cannot write.
Would have the model card declare write authority, re-verified whenever the build fingerprint changes.
States the partition's limits: it protects the record, not the world, and does not reduce confabulation, protect deterministic-layer inputs or keep documentation current.
Comments only on architecture-level controls, claiming not that they cut confabulation but that they bound where errors land and expose each in an incorruptible record.
Defines a write-authority partition holding a component at its declared activity level by construction, inherently safe design in ISO 14971 terms, unlike prompt-based guardrails.
Cites a field report of a prompted rule failing within hours; agrees that labelling cannot move a function along the activity axis, but design can.
Keeps regulatory stratification apart from lifecycle risk management: the partition is a binding characteristic for the first, a control with residual risks for the second.
Agrees the deployed configuration, not the model, is the object of evaluation, and that a master file would not authorize the underlying model.
Agrees substance, not wording, sets directiveness and disclaimers do not lower it; run the other way, inspectable architecture fixes what a function can do.
Agrees risk should be assessed across conversational trajectories, including cumulative drift out of scope.
Agrees adjudicators must be structurally independent, including when the adjudicator is a language model.
Agrees that false confidence and run-to-run variation in safety-critical behaviour are failures, adding that both are better guaranteed by construction than measured by benchmark scores.
Agrees that re-benchmarking should start from the premarket benchmark as baseline, and that third-party model changes are rightly named as a problem.
Welcomes the paper's candour in asking whether premarket uncertainty may be traded for monitoring and whether a machine supervisor is reliable.
Defines the partition by seven verifiable properties: records split by author, an honesty invariant, witnessed closure, computed confidence, reflex stops, passive monitors, a build fingerprint.
Says the framework gauges an output's directiveness but not what the component may do; a component with no write path to fact cannot be action-taking.
Says the partition meets the test that a credited safeguard be binding, verifiable and maintained, and enforces evidence-inference separation by leaving no write path.
Under the partition, conversational drift becomes a logged gate refusal, and a conversational device's intended use is characterized by what its gates permit.
Wants S.3 to distinguish confidence computed over recorded outcomes from model-generated confidence, treating the latter presented as computed as a distinct safety failure.
Proposes a Record Integrity element verifying no write path to the record of fact, surfaced failed predictions and passive monitors, with harness reproducibility tested separately.
Makes the fingerprint the definition of the same device: changes leaving gating and recording layers untouched suit the quality system; changes touching them do not.
Says a fingerprint lets the manufacturer detect a third-party model change without the developer's cooperation, marking when re-benchmarking against the baseline is owed.
Notes the docket divides on postmarket reliance, and says the dispute turns on a question neither side addresses: what the monitoring reads.
Accepts greater premarket uncertainty only where the monitored record is honest by construction, and wants monitoring plans to state every component's write authority.
Would let a supervisory agent read every record yet never write to the record of fact, and pass a passivity test before its readings count.
Says such a record lets clinicians and institutions add signal without taking on accountability, since the record they read stays the manufacturer's responsibility.
Supports agent checkpoints and audit logs, adding three conditions: the agent cannot write the log, gates act on witnessed state, stops stay outside deliberation.
Wants a model-card field declaring what the generative component can and cannot write or initiate, re-verified against the build whenever the fingerprint changes.
Lists the partition's residual risks: no reduction in confabulation, protection of the record not the world, unprotected deterministic inputs, and stale documentation.
Offers a pre-registered, non-clinical research programme with a simple learning agent, showing the partition can be built and tested end to end.
Closes that the paper's strongest commitments point toward controls checkable on the device as built, and casts the partition as what those commitments imply.
